description.value: The study examined whether up- and downregulation of emotion during Ultimatum Game decisions alters behavior and associated brain activity.

spans.text: The aim of the present study was to examine the extent to which decision making in a socially interactive context could be modulated by using emotion regulation strategies, specifically reappraisal.

value: We hypothesized that we would observe lower rejection rates of unfair offers when asked to downregulate, but additionally see higher rejection rates when asked to upregulate, both conditions as compared with baseline.
We hypothesize that, in line with previous work ( Pillutla and Murnighan 1996), anger may be the target emotion involved in UG and the one modulated by the reappraisal strategy.
